_comment: Hand-built payload in the shape JiraClient.search_issues(expand="changelog") returns. Two issues, seven history entries, one items[] entry each. Nothing here is random: every entry stands in for one specific parsing or attribution case, named in its own _comment. tests/apptests/test_changelog_fixture.py pins every field of every parsed row against it, so an attribution regression surfaces as "this row, this field" rather than a frame-shape diff.

issues._comment: The ticket that bounced and healed: resolved, dragged back out, resolved again by a different person. reresolve_events() reads it as 2 resolutions / 1 reopen / hidden_rework, which is exactly the shape a present-tense JQL query for reopened tickets cannot see.

histories._comment: h1 - plain status move, both ends unresolved, named author. The baseline every other entry is a variation on.
h2 - a label-only edit. COSMETIC_FIELDS, not a status move, so is_status is False and from_stage/to_stage are never computed. This is the touch that must not reset a staleness clock.

h3 - the resolving transition. In Progress is not in DEFAULT_RESOLVED_STATUSES; Review in Staging is, which is the whole reason this team can resolve a ticket that is emphatically not done. Credit for this resolution belongs to Priya, the changelog author, not to whoever holds the assignee field today.
h4 - the reopen, straight back out of the resolved status, by someone other than the person who resolved it. The one row reresolve_events() counts as VV-100's reopen.

h5 - the re-resolution: a second, distinct entry into a resolved status on the same ticket. Makes VV-100 count 2 resolutions rather than 1 and marks it hidden_rework, because it is sitting resolved right now and a present-tense query would call it clean.

issues._comment: The clean second ticket, carrying the authorless case. Its resolving move is not its first changelog entry, so the parse is exercised on the ordinary many-transition shape rather than a resolution-on-first-touch special case.

histories._comment: h1 - a plain status move by a bot account, so the resolving entry below is not this ticket's first.

h2 - a resolving transition with the author key absent from the history entry entirely: the deprovisioned-user / some-automation shape. changelog_events() falls back to the "Unknown" sentinel and author_id stays None because there is no author dict to read accountId from. Invisible to credited_resolutions() - there is nobody to credit - which is precisely why unattributed_resolutions() exists to catch it.
